chunks: And Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated from his father, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:

"By God, you, O community of the Shia of the progeny of Muhammad, will be tested like the kohl (ground cosmetic) in the eye. For the owner of the kohl knows when it is put into the eye, but does not know when it leaves. Thus, one of you may be in the morning believing that he is upon our doctrine, and in the evening find that he has left it; and he may be in the evening upon our doctrine, and in the morning find that he has left it."

key_terms.شِيعَةُ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: Shia of the progeny of Muhammad

ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor used to describe the test of faith for Shia during the occultation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) employs the metaphor of kohl (kahl) in the eye to illustrate the subtle, internal trials of faith during the Major Occultation, where adherence to the Imam's teachings may fluctuate imperceptibly. This narration, found in Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, emphasizes that the true test lies not in external persecution but in the spiritual erosion of conviction, requiring constant self-examination to ensure one remains on the path of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 288 - It is narrated from Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Ja’far Himyari from his father from Yaqub bin Yazid from Hammad bin Isa from Ibrahim bin Umar Yamani from a man from Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s) that he said:

“O Shia of Muhammad’s progeny, you are going to be tested like the kohl in the eye. One knows when the kohl is put into his eye, but he does not know when it gets out. In the same way one believes in our matter in the morning and recants it in the evening or believes in it in the evening and when morning comes, he recants it…”
